title: Game 8: Hans vs Magnus
notes: Game 8 of 20 in the experiment. Magnus (the learner) reads his notebook before every move; Hans (the control) has no notebook.

moves.thought: I'll start with the classical e4, controlling the center and opening lines for my bishop and queen.
Standard solid response, controlling the center and preparing development; e5 fights for center space directly.
Developing naturally with the Knight, preparing to control the center and open lines for my pieces.
Standard development, defending e5 pawn and preparing natural development; classic Italian/Ruy Lopez setups follow.
The Ruy Lopez is a strong, classical choice, pressuring the knight defending e5 and developing with purpose.
The Ruy Lopez. Standard reply is a6, challenging the bishop immediately to gain tempo.
Standard Ruy Lopez retreat, maintaining the bishop's pressure on c6 while avoiding exchanges that help Black's development.
Standard Ruy Lopez continuation, developing knight to control center and prepare further development.
Standard Ruy Lopez continuation—castling develops safely and prepares central play.
Standard Ruy Lopez theory; Be7 is the classic Closed Spanish main line, solid and flexible.
Standard Ruy Lopez main line; Re1 supports the e4 pawn and prepares to meet ...b5 lines later.
Standard Closed Ruy Lopez continuation; castling develops safely and prepares central play without weaknesses.
Standard Ruy Lopez development, maintaining the bishop and preparing c3/d4 later. b3 is solid prep for retreating bishop.
Standard Ruy Lopez development, keeping options open and preparing d6/b5 later. Playing the main line response.
Standard Ruy Lopez development, h3 prevents Bg4 pinning my knight and prepares d4 expansion.
Standard Ruy Lopez development; Be6 solidifies, prepares d5 later and eyes the bishop pair trade on a4-e8 diagonal pressure.
Standard Ruy Lopez theory; d3 supports e4, prepares Nbd2, keeps flexible pawn structure in this Closed Ruy Lopez line.
Standard development, keeping solid structure; d5 gains space and challenges center, consistent with normal Ruy Lopez Breyer-like plans.
Standard theory here - capturing exd5 opens the center favorably before Black can advance d4, maintaining pressure.
Recapturing with the knight keeps development active and avoids losing a pawn; Nxd5 centralizes and eyes f4/b4.
I develop my bishop to b3, eyeing the d5 knight and a2-g8 diagonal, maintaining pressure while keeping options open.
Standard development, placing knight actively while eyeing f4; keeps structure solid and avoids weakening moves.
Trading off the strong bishop on e6 simplifies and removes defender; after Bxe6 Nxe6, I can deal with the f4 knight calmly.
Recapturing fxe6 keeps pawn structure solid, opens f-file for rook, and avoids losing material; Nxe6 loses knight to fxe6 anyway equal.
The knight on f4 is annoying; g3 kicks it back and gains space, forcing it to retreat or trade.
Knight on f4 is attacked by g3 pawn; retreating to d5 centralizes safely without losing material.
Rxe5 wins a pawn since Nxe5 is met by Rxe5 attacking the knight on d5 indirectly; actually Rxe5 directly grabs e5 pawn safely.
The rook on e5 attacks my bishop; Bf6 attacks the rook back, forcing it to retreat while developing my bishop safely.
My rook on e5 is attacked by Bf6; Rxe6 escapes while grabbing a pawn safely, since nothing recaptures on e6.
Rook on e6 attacks Nc6 and Bf6 along the rank; Qd7 attacks the rook forcing retreat while staying safe.
My rook on e6 is attacked by the queen; I should retreat it safely rather than trade for a minor piece.
MOVE: Qxh3
My knight attacks the queen on h3, forcing it to retreat and gaining tempo while defending my kingside.
Knight on g5 is undefended; I take it with my bishop, winning a piece for free.
Bishop on g5 is undefended; capturing wins material while neutralizing any mating tricks against my king.
Qh4 attacks the undefended bishop on g5, winning material since nothing guards it.
The queen on h4 is attacked by my bishop on g5; simply capturing wins the queen outright for free.
Material is down; I should activate my rooks on open files rather than risk knight tactics. Rad8 centralizes and pressures d3.
MOVE: Bxd8
I'll recapture the bishop to regain material balance. MOVE: Nxd8
Re8 forks the knight on d8 and rook on f8 along the eighth rank, winning more material.
Rook offers trade; recapturing keeps material balance and avoids losing the rook for free.
I'm up material (rook for bishop/pawn trade favored me heavily). I'll develop and centralize, preparing to consolidate my extra material advantage. MOVE: Nd2
Re1+ forces the king to move and keeps my rook active, maintaining initiative with material advantage.
Simply capturing the rook wins material with no drawback; I'm up a full rook now.
Down material already, I should centralize knight and keep options active rather than passive pawn moves.
I'm up massive material already; grabbing the knight with check simplifies further and leaves me completely winning.
King must move; Kg8 to h8 stays safer from potential future checks along back rank/diagonals, avoiding f-file issues.
Checkmate is available directly with the queen delivering mate on c8.

new_lessons: When a piece is attacked, check all legal capturing moves (not just recaptures) before retreating, since a counter-capture may win material outright.
Before giving an "attacking" check or queen move, verify the target square isn't also guarded by another enemy piece causing a losing exchange.
When your queen or piece dives deep into enemy territory, check all retreat squares are covered, or you risk being trapped and mated.
